items.title: Women abandon football club after sex offender's return
items.description: When a man who sexually assaulted a minor on a post-season football trip was welcomed back to the club with open arms, Megan decided she was done.

items.title: Budget won't be 'main driver' if house prices fall, housing minister says
items.description: The housing minister says the federal budget will have only a "mild" impact on house prices, and if predictions bear out that house prices may drop by 10 per cent, that won't be due to the government's tax changes.

items.title: Police beat a woman in a Sydney street. Their own camera captured their cruelty
items.description: The family of a woman brutally assaulted by police in Sydney has fought to have body-worn camera vision released, in the hope officers will be better trained in responding to acute mental health situations.

items.title: As One Nation broadens its economic appeal, the Liberals return to culture wars
items.description: The Coalition's answer to the rise of conservative populism has been to treat it primarily as a cultural phenomenon. Under Angus Taylor, that instinct appears to be hardening.

items.title: Trump to headline 250th anniversary fair after musicians cancel
items.description: Martina McBride, Bret Michaels, Young MC, Morris Day and The Time and The Commodores all said they would not perform after alleging they were misled about the nature of the event.

items.title: Why are Australians still getting lost and dying in the outback?
items.description: Kelly’s son and ex-husband died "stupid" deaths in the Australian outback. She’s on a mission to make sure no more lives are lost.

items.title: Live: Socceroos' last chance before World Cup squad selection against Mexico
items.description: Australia's World Cup hopefuls get one final chance to impress before the Socceroos' squad for the 2026 World Cup is finalised against Mexico at the Rose Bowl. Follow live.

items.title: Dozens of arrests during Champions League celebrations on Paris streets
items.description: Celebrations of Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory have turned violent, as fans clashed with police on the streets of the French capital.

items.title: Surrounded by smoke in pregnancy, mothers fear it made their babies sick
items.description: Years after bushfires covered their cities in smoke, mothers are left wondering if their children's chronic illnesses began with what was in the air before they were born.

items.title: Flotilla activists take evidence of alleged abuse to international court
items.description: Eleven Australians detained by Israeli forces while attempting to deliver aid to Gaza have submitted evidence to the International Criminal Court alleging abuse, torture and other violations during their detention.

items.title: At 15 Mohamed Semra made headlines. At 27 he’s making history
items.description: At just 27, Mohamed Semra is not your average mayor. He overcame a childhood stutter and a viral moment in a Melbourne Apple Store to make political history – and he is just getting started.

items.title: Rare images capture pioneer life on WA's south coast in the early 1900s
items.description: Pioneering photographer Bert Saw captured Federation-era life and experiences in Denmark, Albany and surrounding communities throughout the 1900s.

items.title: The 'bread and butter' of a local court: More than 20 names on the traffic list
items.description: From hoons to drink drivers to people driving without a licence, one magistrate is trying to make sure the people brought before her know how quickly things can turn deadly on the roads.

items.title: Love story: Locking down the 'one that got away'
items.description: For a long time, I considered my teenage crush the one that got away. That all changed when we reconnected two decades later.

items.title: As Jane Austen turns 250, four new productions take on Pride and Prejudice
items.description: In a modern-day cost-of-living crisis, the classic 1817 novel's tale of inheritance and wealth still rings true.

items.title: After five days in a dark cave, a scientist emerged with life-changing insights
items.description: Spending big money to do nothing in the dark is on the rise. Scientist Kiana Aran chronicled what happened to her when she tried it.

items.title: Former teachers' pets, rejoice. Guy Montgomery's spelling quiz is back
items.description: Welcome back to your Sunday morning quiz with everyone's favourite word wonderboy.

items.title: Is the government really overhauling employment services?
items.description: The government isn't rebuilding the Commonwealth Employment Service, but will its proposed changes fix a broken system?

items.title: The end came quickly for Madeleine Ogilvie, who jumped before being pushed
items.description: It started with a seemingly innocuous question. Over the course of several months, Madeleine Ogilvie had many opportunities to provide clarification, but didn't until last week. Then the end came quickly.

items.title: Police find 11yo boy who went missing in wild weather in Perth
items.description: An 11-year-old autistic boy, who is non-verbal, has been found after going missing from Perth's western suburbs in wild weather on Saturday afternoon.

items.title: 'Losing a generation': Why some countries are moving fast on AI in schools
items.description: Countries in Asia are emerging as the world's early adopters of AI in education, as the global race to lead in the technology accelerates.

items.title: How clay-court chaos is a return to the norm at the French Open
items.description: All the key favourites are now out of the men's draw at the French Open, but then again, this tournament has always been just a little bit different.

items.title: AUKUS partners unveil plan to develop underwater drones
items.description: The US, Australia and United Kingdom have unveiled a new "signature" project to develop cutting edge weapons systems and sensors for underwater drones as they try to reinvigorate the second pillar of the AUKUS agreement.

items.title: This preacher was once part of NZ's gang world. Now he's trying to heal it
items.description: In a country where there now more gang members than police officers, a former gang member turned Christian pastor is trying to turn things around for others by addressing the root causes of gang life.

items.title: How Tiananmen Square vigils in Hong Kong have become unlawful
items.description: In May, Hong Kong's High Court began hearing closing arguments in the case of two democracy activists charged with inciting subversion for organising a candlelight vigil to remember Tiananmen Square.
